research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11549 (35 FR 12191, Federal Register of July 30, 1970; the govinfo PDF text layer), headed Executive Order 11549, Revoking Executive Order No. 10361 of June 11, 1952, Establishing the Whittier Defensive Sea Area, Alaska, signed by Richard Nixon and dated July 28, 1970 (filed July 28, 1970); number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: the order is a single sentence under section 2152 of title 18, United States Code, by which Executive Order No. 10361 is revoked. The dossier's single whole-order clause matches. Lifecycle: the command is a one-time revocation performed when the order took effect. The order has no effective-date wording, so it took effect on signing, 1970-07-28; the printing date 1970-07-30 is an alternative reading, not an end. The clause is exhausted by performance on 1970-07-28. Searches: the U.S. Code, eCFR and Office of the Federal Register disposition-note searches record no hit for this order; a held-corpus search by number returns only this order's own printings; the order is not in the table of EO 12553. No amendment, revocation or supersession of this order is held.
savings_reason: The order contains no savings, exception, effective-date or notwithstanding wording; the held text was read in full. The revocation of EO 10361 was complete on 1970-07-28. Whatever the defensive sea area established by EO 10361 did before that date was an effect of the revoked order, not a command of this one; nothing in the held evidence shows a continuing right or duty arising from this order.
earlier_end_check: Checked for an earlier end: the order is dated July 28, 1970 and its only command is performed on taking effect, so no earlier instrument can have ended it. No later instrument in the held corpus names Executive Order 11549 (number search of held texts, forms Executive Order No., Ex. Ord., E.O.).
scope_check: The whole order is one clause with one revoking command, with no condition, exception or term; no partial revocation, amendment or suspension of any part is held.
independent_command_check: The order creates no office, delegation, fund, right or duty of its own; its only command is the revocation of EO 10361, performed at once. The statute it cites (18 U.S.C. 2152) is not a command of the order.
savings_check: No savings wording appears in the order and none is added by any held later instrument; no continuing right or duty arising from the order is shown.

research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11568 (35 FR 17703, Federal Register of November 18, 1970; the govinfo PDF text layer, whose heading reads 11568 with the name garbled as MadNTYRE), Exempting A. Everette MacIntyre from compulsory retirement for age, signed by Richard Nixon and dated November 16, 1970 (filed November 16, 1970); number, date and subject agree with the census register, and the text of Executive Order 11642 independently names this order by number and date. Inventory: two recitals (MacIntyre, a member of the Federal Trade Commission, will become subject to compulsory retirement under 5 U.S.C. 8335 during February 1971; the public interest requires the exemption) and one operative command exempting him from compulsory retirement for age until February 29, 1972. The dossier's single whole-order clause matches. Lifecycle: the exemption ends by its own terms on the stated date. Under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling on until-dates the end is recorded inclusive, 1972-02-29 (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading is that it ends when that day begins. Later event: Executive Order 11642, signed 1972-02-01 (37 FR 2565), recites this order and exempts MacIntyre further, until February 28, 1973; it is a new grant that overlaps the last four weeks of this one, does not revoke or shorten it, and is recorded as a later event with its own date and quote, not as this order's end. Searches: the U.S. Code and eCFR searches record no hit for this order; the Office of the Federal Register disposition-note search records one hit, the later further exemption; the held-text person-name search records no other hit. The dossier's missing item for the target provision of EO 11642 is resolved by reading EO 11642 in full: it is a further grant, not an amendment of this order's text.
savings_reason: The order contains no savings or continuation wording. The exemption expired by its own terms on 1972-02-29 and was followed by a separate grant in Executive Order 11642; actions taken while the exemption ran were completed acts. No continuing right or duty arising from this order after its term is shown in held evidence.
earlier_end_check: Checked for an earlier end: no held instrument revokes, shortens or amends Executive Order 11568. Executive Order 11642 (1972-02-01) is the only held later order naming it; it recites this order and grants a further exemption until February 28, 1973, so it extends coverage and ends nothing. The until-date February 29, 1972 is the first end, recorded inclusive with the exclusive alternative disclosed.
scope_check: The whole order is one clause concerning one named person with one fixed term; no partial amendment or revocation of any part is held, and the later further exemption is a new grant that touches no text of this order.
independent_command_check: The order has no command independent of the exemption: it creates no office, fund, delegation or right apart from the exemption itself, and the statute it cites (5 U.S.C. 8335(c)) is not a command of the order. The recitals are not commands.
savings_check: No savings wording appears in the order. The later further exemption is a separate instrument with its own term; nothing in the held evidence shows a continuing right or duty arising from this order after 1972-02-29.
